blocks.task_summary: Find the smallest possible perimeter of triangle ABC given two sides and a non-included angle (ambiguous case), by applying cosine or sine rule, obtaining two possible third-side lengths, and selecting the acute case that minimises the perimeter.
method_path: Apply cosine rule: 7^2 = 12^2 + AB^2 - 2*12*AB*cos 25 deg, or sine rule: sin B/12 = sin 25 deg/7
Solve for AB (quadratic) or angles B and C, obtaining two possible values from the ambiguous case
Select the smaller AB (acute angle C) to minimise the perimeter
accepted_alternatives: Cosine rule route: set up 7^2 = 12^2 + AB^2 - 2*12*AB*cos 25 deg, solve quadratic AB^2 - 21.7513...*AB + 95 = 0, take smaller root AB approx 6.05068, perimeter = 12 + 7 + 6.05068 approx 25.1

Sine rule route: sin B/12 = sin 25 deg/7 gives sin B approx 0.724488, B approx 46.4263 deg or 133.573 deg, then C = 180 deg - 25 deg - B gives acute C approx 21.4263 deg, find AB via sine or cosine rule, perimeter approx 25.1

evidence.basis: Full markscheme for Q2: EITHER cosine rule (M1)(A1)(A1)(M1)A1 or OR sine rule (M1)(A1)(A1)(M1) THEN A1; final answer minimum perimeter = 25.1

evidence.basis: recognize that the variable has a Binomial distribution (M1); attempt to find P(X ≥ 1) (M1); 1 − P(X = 0) OR 1 − 0.95^30 OR 1 − 0.214638... OR 0.785361... ; P(X ≥ 1) = 0.785 A1

accepted_alternatives: Compute numerator as P(X ≤ 2) − P(X = 0) ≈ 0.81218 − 0.21464 = 0.59754
Compute numerator as P(X = 1) + P(X = 2) ≈ 0.33890 + 0.25864 = 0.59754

blocks.task_summary: Given a semicircle with centre O, radius r, points P, Q, R on the circumference with PQ = 2r and ∠ROQ = θ, and the two shaded regions having equal area, show that θ = 2 sin θ.
method_path: Express area of segment bounded by chord RQ and arc RQ as ½r²θ − ½r² sin θ
Express area of triangle POR as ½r² sin(π − θ)
Set areas equal: ½r²θ − ½r² sin θ = ½r² sin(π − θ)
Cancel ½r² and apply sin(π − θ) = sin θ
Obtain θ − sin θ = sin θ → θ = 2 sin θ
accepted_alternatives: Directly state area of triangle POR as ½r² sin θ (simplifying sin(π − θ) immediately), award maximum M1A1A0A1A1 per markscheme

evidence.basis: attempt to find the area of either shaded region in terms of r and θ (M1); Area of segment = ½r²θ − ½r² sin θ A1; Area of triangle = ½r² sin(π − θ) A1; correct equation in terms of θ only (A1); θ − sin θ = sin θ → θ = 2 sin θ A1 [5 marks]

evidence.basis: 1.89549… → θ = 1.90 A1; Note: Award A0 if there is more than one solution. Award A0 for an answer in degrees. [1 mark]

blocks.task_summary: Prove the polynomial identity (p+q)³ − 3pq(p+q) ≡ p³ + q³.
accepted_alternatives: METHOD 2: Factorise (p+q)³ − 3pq(p+q) = (p+q)[(p+q)² − 3pq] = (p+q)(p² − pq + q²) then expand to p³ + q³.
METHOD 3: Factorise p³ + q³ = (p+q)(p² − pq + q²) = (p+q)[(p+q)² − 3pq] = (p+q)³ − 3pq(p+q).

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: M1 for attempts to expand (p+q)³; A1 for correct simplification to p³+q³ AG. METHOD 2: M1 for attempts to factorise (p+q)³−3pq(p+q); A1 for correct expansion to p³+q³. METHOD 3: M1 for attempts to factorise p³+q³; A1 for correct rewriting as (p+q)³−3pq(p+q).

blocks.task_summary: Show by implicit differentiation that (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0 for the curve y = x − xy ln(xy), x > 0, y > 0.
method_path: Differentiate y = x − xy ln(xy) implicitly, applying product rule and chain rule to xy ln(xy)
Collect all dy/dx terms on one side
Algebraically rearrange to obtain (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: rewrite as y/x = 1 − ln(xy) − y ln(xy) then differentiate implicitly
Method 3: treat (x ln(xy)) and y as separate factors via product rule
Method 4: substitute w = xy, differentiate w.r.t. x using dy/dx = dw/dx relation, then simplify

evidence.basis: M1: attempts to differentiate implicitly including at least one application of the product rule
A1: correct differentiation and simplification to the required form
A1: final line (1+ln(xy))(dy/dx)+(1+y/x)=1 leading to AG

blocks.task_summary: Hence find the equation of the tangent to C at the point where x = 1.
method_path: Substitute x = 1 into y = x − xy ln(xy) to obtain y = 1 − y ln y and solve y = 1
Substitute x = 1, y = 1 into the differentiated result (1 + ln(xy)) dy/dx + (1 + y/x) = 0
accepted_alternatives: Method 2: substitute x = 1 into the derivative relation first, then use y = 1 − y ln y to determine dy/dx = 0, then find y = 1 and tangent y = 1

evidence.basis: M1: substitutes x = 1 into y = x − xy ln(xy)
A1: y = 1 − y ln y ⇒ y = 1
M1: substitutes x = 1 and their non-zero value of y into the derivative expression
A1: dy/dx = 0
A1: equation of the tangent is y = 1
